title: feat(cli,runtime): os dev upgrades a v17-shape development database in place; the ownership ceremony covers the telemetry sibling and adopts legacy shipped-set seeds (ADR-0131)
body:
## Why

On two long-lived 17.x development databases (hotcrm's and the showcase's), the v18 boot refuses to start ("still in the v17 organization-ownership shape … Run 'os migrate organization-ownership'"), and the prescribed ceremony then fails in sequence:

1. `sys_scim_provider` has no inventory row, so the plan refuses. That fix is **#23874**, not this PR.
2. Run from a shell without `NODE_ENV=development`, the ceremony composes no security plugin and no audit plugin. Its authored-conversion step blocks on the shipped permission sets, and its column-drops step blocks on `sys_audit_log` ("declares no object").
3. Installs created before the 2026-08-15 seeder ruling store the eight shipped permission sets as `managed_by: 'admin'`. They read as Setup-authored, and every one whose stored body differs from the shipped definition is refused with "rename the authored row".
4. A development boot keeps the lifecycle objects (`sys_audit_log`, `sys_job_run`, `sys_notification`, …) in the `telemetry` sibling. The boot guard reads their columns there, but the ceremony read only the primary, so an upgraded database still never booted. Stale copies of those tables in the primary also blocked column-drops, with the misleading message "run the release whose declaration drops it".

The maintainer's ruling for this PR (2026-10-16, recorded verbatim in the ADR-0131 amendment): customers' temporary development data must not cost them effort; production data must not go wrong, so production gets warnings. The ruling chose: `os dev` completes the upgrade itself; adopt the legacy seeds automatically; full coverage of the telemetry sibling; add `--dev` to the ceremony.

## What changes

- **`os dev` upgrades a v17-shape local SQLite development database in place.** The refused `serve --dev` child tells its parent over IPC and exits. The parent copies the database and its `telemetry` sibling (with `-wal`/`-shm`) to `<data dir>/backups/organization-ownership-<ts>/`, runs `os migrate organization-ownership --dev` (plan), applies that plan, and boots again only when the report says `complete`. It runs once per session. A blocked step ends `os dev` with the blocker, where the copy is, and how to resume. `os serve` / `os start` and any non-file database keep the refusal unchanged. (`utils/dev-organization-ownership-upgrade.ts`; `ServeRestartCoordinator` gains `recover`.)
- **Warnings.** The plan carries `warnings` (and `staleCopies`). The plan prints them, `--apply` prints them again before its first write (`onWarning`), and the apply report keeps them.
- **Each object in its own database.** `buildOrganizationOwnershipPlan` / `applyOrganizationOwnership` take `siblings` and `homeOf` (the booted engine's routing). Tables are planned, attributed and column-dropped where they live, and anchors are read where theirs live (a sibling notification takes its organization from a record in the primary). A table in a database its object no longer lives in is listed under `staleCopies`, warned about, and never touched.
- **Legacy shipped-set seeds.** `LEGACY_SHIPPED_SET_SEEDS` (`managed_by='admin'` and a name in `SHIPPED_PERMISSION_SET_NAMES`, pinned equal to plugin-security's `securityDefaultPermissionSets`) is a new `sys_permission_set` category in the plan. At the start of authored-conversion those rows are re-owned `platform`, so the existing mirror-deletion removes them once the rewrite has named every grant.
- **`--dev` on the ceremony.** It boots the stack as `os serve --dev` does (`serveFlags.dev` for both boots and the occupancy probe). `composeServedPlatform` now reads `serveFlags.dev` for the auth secret's development fallback; before, it read `isDevelopmentBoot(undefined)`, so `--dev` alone composed no auth family and no `sys_audit_log`. A development boot's refusal names the command with `--dev` (`OrganizationOwnershipBootGuardPlugin({ dev })`).
- **The boot refusal names an apply the ceremony accepts**: `--out PLAN`, then `--apply --plan-file PLAN --backup-taken`. A bare `--apply` is refused without a reviewed plan file.
- **ADR-0131** gains the 2026-10-16 amendment. The D10 text names the one exception to "never an automatic boot step".

Unchanged on purpose: the `declared-rule-mirrors` departure still counts in the post-check until the declared-rule seeder retires, as its CHANGELOG entry says. After a full run the boot guard no longer needs the marker, because no v17 column is left.

## Verification

- New suites: `organization-ownership-plan.siblings.integration.test.ts` (6), `organization-ownership-apply.siblings.test.ts` (3), `dev-organization-ownership-upgrade.test.ts` (5), coordinator `recover` cases in `dev-restart.test.ts` (4), the shipped-name pin in `organization-ownership-inventory.test.ts`, and the `--dev` refusal in `organization-ownership-boot-guard.test.ts`. The existing ceremony suites (15 files, 205 tests) pass unchanged.
- End to end, on a copy of the showcase's real 17.x dev database (with its telemetry sibling), using this branch's CLI:
  - `os migrate organization-ownership --dev` plans 9 tables `[telemetry]` and warns about the 8 legacy sets.
  - `--apply` completes all 9 steps. 37,923 rows are attributed (9,406 notifications in the sibling among them), the 8 seeds are adopted and deleted, and 13 columns are dropped, including the sibling's.
  - `os serve --dev` then boots (health 200).
- End to end, `os dev` on a fresh copy of the same database (the empty `sys_scim_provider` dropped, standing in for #23874): it prints `⟳ … upgrading it in place`, then the warning, then `✓ Upgraded … copied to …/backups/organization-ownership-…`, then `✓ server started on the upgraded database`, and health returns 200. The backup dir holds the copy, `plan.json`, `apply.json` and `ceremony.log`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime typecheck`, and eslint on the changed files are clean.

Fixes #23871
Fixes #23872
Fixes #23873 (ruled 2026-10-16: adopt them automatically, and warn in production; recorded verbatim in the ADR-0131 amendment)

Depends on #23874 for databases that still hold `sys_scim_provider`: without that inventory row, the plan refuses before any of this runs.

Local test note: the full `@objectstack/cli` suite on macOS fails 7 files for environment reasons only: `/private/var` vs `/var` tmpdir paths, the local Asia/Taipei timezone in `verify-dashboard-windows`, and no util-linux `script(1)` for `dev-boot-output-order`. None of these touches this diff; CI on Linux is the judge.
